criteria.claim: The show is long-form and built around unusual people, unconventional ideas, crime, addiction, UFOs and classified programs, health, tech and consciousness.
Stated mission: bring fringe cultures to a wider audience through storytelling and cinematography.
Past guests range from CERN physicists to professional casino cheats, erotic hypnotists and Olympic athletes.

The show has already covered the art world: episode #346, 'The $450 Million Da Vinci Conspiracy & CIA Psyops Behind Modern Art' with Giampiero Ambrosi, covering forger Tony Tetro and James Stunt's fake art.
No interview was found in which Danny explains how he picks guests, and no Reddit guest-request evidence was found.

logistics.claim: Danny Jones is a filmmaker based in Florida.
The exact studio city was not confirmed. The Tampa Bay Chronicle tied a Tampa reference only to a guest who traveled there to appear, so Tampa is likely but unverified.
Episodes frequently run more than 2 to 3 hours.
As of August 2026: about 1.28M YouTube subscribers, 186M views, 650+ videos and 420+ episodes since 2018. The show was formerly called Koncrete Podcast.

what_works.claim: Guests who can unfold a detailed first-hand account across a long conversation.
Conspiracy, crime and money angles inside niche worlds: the art-forgery/CIA episode shows the art world fits when it is framed as hidden-world intrigue.

what_fails.claim: Generic business or self-promo pitches with no fringe, insider or story angle are unlikely to land, given the stated mission.

Buzzsprout 2026 survey of 271 podcasters on where guests come from: personal network 69.7%, social media 28.4%, cold email pitch 28.0%, referrals from past guests 28.0%, guest platforms 22.5%, PR agency 19.9%, listeners 18.1%, events 13.7%, online communities 11.8% (multiple answers allowed).
Podchaser 2026: median pitch acceptance rate is 5% and median response rate is 17.5%. Well-matched pitches get about 70% positive host responses.
A mediocre pitch to a sharply targeted list converts at 25 to 35%. A perfect pitch to a poorly targeted list converts at 3 to 5%.

PodMatch costs about $6 to $64 a month and uses algorithmic matching, skewing to entrepreneurship and SaaS. MatchMaker.fm costs about $129 a year, has a free tier and skews to wellness, social impact and international shows.
Shows like Danny Jones, Julian Dorey and Whiskey Ginger do not appear to book through PodMatch or MatchMaker. Those platforms suit smaller shows. Use them for volume, not for top-tier targets.
Podchaser Pro lists 2.19M+ contacts by role (host, producer, talent booker) on each show's Insights tab.
Rephonic scrapes emails from websites, RSS and databases, flags verified and likely-invalid contacts, and lets users vote on contact quality.

Pre-calls typically run 15 to 30 minutes. Producers check for natural storytelling versus canned talking points, and topics or questions are often sent about a week ahead. Hosts send assets (links, pre-written posts, a clip, a quote graphic) and expect guests to share. Guests who don't share get noticed.
Avery should commit to sharing to his and Alec Monopoly's social accounts and to ArtLife channels.
AI-generated template pitches are the top reason for an instant no, cited by 68% of producers. Some producers block whole sending domains.
Wrong fit accounts for 36% of declines. Other red flags: generic pitches with no show reference, form emails with repeated follow-ups, and bragging about stats.

Scams ask for a 'production', 'editing' or 'booking' fee before the interview. Some real shows charge up to $50,000 per slot. Vet the show's real audience, and be wary of Gmail-only hosts who claim ties to famous shows.
Some invites lead to fake 'tech checks' meant to take over social accounts.

Send on Tuesday or Wednesday, 8 to 10am in the host's time zone. Mondays are buried, and Thursday and Friday responses are lower.
